category_title: Student with learning disabilities who whines and refuses to work
minimal_context: Irene is assigned an independent math worksheet in the pull-out special education classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is your math worksheet for today. Please complete these problems independently.

STUDENT: (Whining) I don't want to do this math worksheet, it looks too hard.

TUTOR: Just look at the first problem and try your best.

STUDENT: I can't do it! I never get these right.

TUTOR: I need you to work on this by yourself for the next ten minutes.

STUDENT: (Loudly pushes the desk) No! I'm not doing it! I'm not doing any of this work!

options.A: Agree with the student that they are having a rough time with the independent math worksheet during this session.
options.B: Set a timer to buzz on a fixed 1-minute interval schedule and provide specific performance feedback based on the student's behavior (e.g., 'great job working').
options.C: Simplify the instructions for the independent math worksheet before asking the student to attempt the first problem.
options.D: Ask a follow-up question that links the student's physical sensation to a potential emotional state regarding the math worksheet.
